runtime: Shared content-addressed KTX2/UASTC surfaces, with retained 2K desktop and 512px fallback derivatives. Architectural UV revision 3 and physical grain scale are retained. Four interpreted colour profiles, separate authored Bedford maps, restrained normal strength and material-specific roughness/optics are applied by the appearance library. Runtime encoding and sampled-channel preservation are documented in the asset reports; original CC0 source files remain unchanged. Desktop is the focus of this iteration; additional mobile optimization is deferred.
lighting: Completed Phase4 neutral-dome Cycles illumination uses8192px for the waiting-room vault,4096px for masonry and colossal order, and2048px for exterior/concourse/platform. The repaired order uses512 Metal samples; other atlases128, with six diffuse bounces. The order retains4096px desktop AO. All final inputs include the broad revision3 prism court and repaired leaf source; each report records actual source/occluder hashes. Fine ironwork and repeated tiny concrete webs remain outside the large masonry atlas. Directional sun stays dynamic. Explicit linear-radiance transfer and pixel-identical lossless WebP preserve the normalized atlas; the browser restores scale and irradiance. Completed settings do not establish final photographic fidelity or calibrated historic colours.
reflections: Four completed repaired-source static captures use2048x1024 HDR,64 Metal samples, plus512x256 low derivatives. Non-Color resizing and zero dither preserve linear radiance. assets/reflection-probes.json and reflection-exterior-probe.json retain source hashes, positions and decoded transport identity. Static probes have no positional parallax, moving-passenger reflections or time-specific indirect relighting. Sky, colours, sun and exposure are not historically calibrated.
denoising: Color-only OpenImageDenoise filters explicitly linear radiance; runtime sRGB is encoded once and transported as lossless WebP. Original and denoised full-resolution HDR are losslessly gzip archived under authoring/penn-station-1935/lighting/phase4, with decoded SHA verification. Each atlas records its0.18 control, radiance statistics and clipping. Filtering can soften fine features; mapped browser review remains separately required.

appearance.scope: Four interpreted colour derivatives and reduced normal strengths retain the original nine ambientCG maps and architectural UV revision3. The broader visual pass also introduces separately authored seamless Bedford maps, an interpreted InteriorGranite roughness factor 0.50 and distinct milky opal-glass response; global illumination and static probes are freshly rebuilt rather than retained from the maintenance checkpoint.
appearance.method: Decode sRGB to linear; normalize each source channel by its spatial mean; apply contrast about that mean and multiply by the target linear palette; clip to0..1; resize in linear light; encode sRGB once.
appearance.baseColourFactors: Original material-family factors are accounted for in the colour-derivative application reports. The authored Bedford maps already contain their target mean linear colour and use a unit baseColorFactor, avoiding double tinting.
appearance.lightingLimitation: The maintenance checkpoint retained Phase3 lighting. The completed visual pass rebuilds all six illumination atlases and four static probes with recorded final geometry/material inputs. Transfer validation and mapped visual acceptance are separate; historic colour, polish, lamp photometry and weather remain uncalibrated.
appearance.interiorGraniteFinish: The smoother shaft response is interpreted from primary photographs; 0.50 is a material multiplier on the existing modern roughness map, not a measured historic polish specification.

application.uvScale: ArchitecturalUV stores0.28UV/m before material preparation; use UV/(0.28*1.5) for a1.5m tile. Do not apply the colour(.56,.55,.49) a second time.
